sec:transfer-matrix-mass-intro:
The categorical mass endomorphism assigns an algebraic invariant to each braid closure, yet a physical mass spectrum requires an operator that propagates local crossing weights along a closed worldline and extracts a level-independent trace. Within the five-step categorical pipeline—from the braided monoidal category through the Iwahori–Hecke algebra H_n(q), the Bring-surface geometry, and the archimedean period realization \tau_{\mathrm{arch}} to physical spectra—this chapter constructs the mass functional and traces its four mathematical faces:

  1. Arc I (Algebraic and Transfer-Matrix Foundations) compiles vertex operators into the categorical transfer matrix, establishes level independence across the brane tower, decomposes the Markov trace over Wedderburn blocks under the three-calibration discipline, and anchors the normal-form reduction in the Gröbner–Shirshov axioms.
  2. Arc II (Geometric and Archimedean Realization) factors vertex operators through the exceptional divisor \mathcal{S}_p, identifies the quantum dilogarithm \mathrm{Li}_2^q as the Kashiwara–Jones crystal cocycle, constructs the archimedean realization \tau_{\mathrm{arch}} to Kashaev hyperbolic volume, and develops the \varphi_q resummation and depth-3 cyclotomic trilogarithm identities.
  3. Arc III (Many-Body Nuclear Binding, Cumulants, and the Wenzl Bridge) formulates nuclear binding via linear-programming shadow prices and Jucys–Murphy central elements, establishes the canonical torus-chain closure and subset-cumulant recursion, and connects the Plancherel measure to closed-form Wenzl weights y_\lambda and Geer–Patureau-Mirand–Turaev (GPMT) modified quantum dimensions.
  4. Arc IV (Elementary Particle and Gauge Coupling Derivations) resolves the classical mirror-parity blindness via Frobenius codimension, derives the six-term mass formula and crystal isospin splitting, and evaluates single-particle and composite spectra across the real binding component \operatorname{Re}\mathfrak{V} and the imaginary decay component \operatorname{Im}\mathfrak{V}.

This opening section constructs the categorical transfer matrix by assembling vertex morphisms across the brane-tower state space. Operator level independence ensures that the Markov trace remains invariant under level shifts, while the constituent-and-composite agreement lemma proves that constituent strand factorisation coincides with composite link evaluation. In the smooth locus, the topological mass formula expresses the categorical mass through the motivic mass measure \mu and the Hecke mass element in H_n(q), with the hyperbolic volumes it involves conjecturally algebraically independent, whose Frobenius self-pairing establishes charge–mass duality and whose skein decomposition governs the nuclear knot classification and scattering pipeline.
def:categorical-transfer-matrix:
Definition Categorical transfer matrix. Let \mathfrak{H}_p = [K_1, \ldots, K_n]_p \oplus \mathcal{L} be a hadron at a brane point p (localized hadron), and let \mathcal{S}_p be the exceptional divisor at p (exceptional divisor).

A categorical transfer matrix for \mathfrak{H}_p is the equivalence class

  \mathcal{T}(\mathfrak{H})
  = 
  \bigl[ T \bigr]_{\sim}
   \in 
  \mathrm{End}\bigl(H_n(R, q)\bigr) \big/ \sim

where T is any braiding operation on \mathfrak{H} (at either level) and the equivalence relation \sim identifies two operations T_1 \sim T_2 whenever they produce the same vertex volume:

  T_1 \sim T_2
  \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
  \hat{V}(T_1, q) = \hat{V}(T_2, q)
  \quad\text{as polynomials in } q.
prop:transfer-matrix-level-independence:
Proposition Transfer matrix level independence. Conditional on Hecke normal forms realise crystal highest-weight vectors. Let \mathfrak{H}_p = [K_1, \ldots, K_n]_p \oplus \mathcal{L} be a hadron with composite knot K_{\mathfrak{H}} = \hat{\beta}_{\mathfrak{H}}. Let \mathcal{T}(\mathfrak{H}_p) be the categorical transfer matrix (categorical transfer matrix). Then:

  1. Constituent-composite agreement. The composite invariant is derived from the constituents rather than independent of them: the Markov trace computed from the constituent insertion points (z_1, \ldots, z_n) is the composite invariant, so two hadrons with the same constituents have the same composite. Concretely,

      \prod_{i=0}^{n-2} \hat{V}_i^{\mathrm{const}}(q)
  = 
  \hat{V}^{\mathrm{comp}}(q)
  = 
  J_{K_{\mathfrak{H}}}(q).

  2. Path independence on \mathcal{S}_p. Two braiding operations T_1, T_2 on \mathfrak{H} that produce isotopy-equivalent configurations have the same categorical transfer matrix: \mathcal{T}(T_1) = \mathcal{T}(T_2). In particular, the specific sequence of crossing changes within the exceptional divisor \mathcal{S}_p does not affect the result --- only the equivalence class of the final configuration matters.

  3. Well-definedness. The categorical transfer matrix \mathcal{T}(\mathfrak{H}) depends only on the isotopy class of the hadron \mathfrak{H} and the knot types K_i of its constituents. It is independent of:

    • the braid representative \beta_{\mathfrak{H}},
    • the PawLei embedding \iota_{j_i} for each constituent,
    • the order of crossings evaluated within \mathcal{S}_p.

conj:topological-mass-formula:
Conjecture Topological mass formula (Archimedean). Let (\mathbf{C}, A, \tau) be the \mathbb{C}-quantum observable universe and let K be a hyperbolic knot whose complement carries the vortex topology of a stable particle, generated by N blow-ups along the brane tower. It is conjectured that the mass formula

  \mathfrak{m}(K) = \frac{\mathrm{Vol}(K)}{\hbar_q^{2}}

holds, where \mathrm{Vol}(K) is the hyperbolic volume of S^3 \setminus K and \hbar_q = 1 - 1/q is the quantum Planck constant (quantum Planck constant) at the substrate parameter q (substrate parameter). The descent involution \hat{\tau}_n (descent involution) induces the idempotent splitting \mathrm{End}_{\mathbf{C}}(A_{n+1}) = \mathcal{A}^{\mathrm{desc}} \oplus \mathcal{A}^{\mathrm{trans}} (descent eigenspaces); under the archimedean fibre functor, the descended trace evaluates to the holonomy \mathrm{Hol}_{\nabla_A} and each transient trace to the quantum dilogarithm \Phi_q(z_i).

The archimedean-realisation framing of this closed form is described in the topological mass-formula context.
rem:topological-mass-formula-context: Remark Archimedean-realisation framing of the topological mass formula. In the archimedean realisation (\mathbb{C}-quantum observable universe), the topological decomposition of mass (topological mass) specialises to a closed-form relationship between the mass of a particle, the hyperbolic volume of its associated knot, and the quantum Planck constant.
conj:hyperbolic-volume-transcendence:
Conjecture Algebraic independence of QOU hyperbolic volumes. The topological mass formula assigns mass \mathfrak{m}(K) = \mathrm{Vol}(K)/\hbar_q^2. Here q denotes the substrate parameter. Three non-zero hyperbolic volumes drive the Descartes universe mass spectrum:

Knot/Link Volume QOU identity
Figure-eight 4_1 \mathrm{Vol}(4_1) = 2\,\mathrm{Cl}_2(\pi/3) \approx 2.02988 Higgs boson
Three-twist 5_2 \mathrm{Vol}(5_2) \approx 2.82812 Down quark
Borromean rings \mathcal{B}_3 \mathrm{Vol}(\mathcal{B}_3) \approx 7.32772 Nucleon

All torus knots (trefoil, cinquefoil, septafoil) possess zero hyperbolic volume. They contribute no topological mass from this channel.

The set \{\mathrm{Vol}(4_1),\; \mathrm{Vol}(5_2),\; \mathrm{Vol}(\mathcal{B}_3)\} is algebraically independent over \mathbb{Q}[q, q^{-1}]. There exists no non-zero polynomial P \in \mathbb{Q}[q, q^{-1}][x, y, z] satisfying

  P\bigl(\mathrm{Vol}(4_1),\; \mathrm{Vol}(5_2),\;
    \mathrm{Vol}(\mathcal{B}_3)\bigr) = 0.

If the conjecture holds, the physical coefficient ring of the Descartes universe forms \mathbb{Q}[q, q^{-1}][\mathrm{Vol}(4_1),\allowbreak \mathrm{Vol}(5_2),\allowbreak \mathrm{Vol}(\mathcal{B}_3)]. This defines a polynomial ring in three transcendentals over the ground ring. The specialisation map \iota \colon \mathbb{Z}[q, q^{-1}] \to \mathbb{R} sending q \mapsto q_0 extends to an embedding of this ring into \mathbb{R}. The three volumes remain algebraically independent over \mathbb{Q}(q_0).

Remark. The irrationality of a single hyperbolic 3-manifold volume remains an open problem. The Borel--Zagier conjecture concerns only \mathbb{Q}-linear independence of volumes of non-commensurable manifolds. This presents a strictly weaker, yet unresolved, claim. Reid (1991) established 4_1 as the unique arithmetic hyperbolic knot, commensurable with \mathrm{PSL}_2(\mathcal{O}_3). The three-twist 5_2 is non-arithmetic. The Borromean rings \mathcal{B}_3, as a 3-component link, fall outside Reid's classification. The three complements are pairwise non-commensurable. The Borel--Zagier conjecture would thus guarantee their \mathbb{Q}-linear independence.

Scope: external open problem, partial categorical approach. This conjecture remains external to the framework. Its three forms

  \text{irrationality}
  \;\Longleftarrow\;
  \mathbb{Q}\text{-linear independence}
  \;\Longleftarrow\;
  \text{algebraic independence}

represent recognised open problems in transcendental number theory. The framework specifies only the choice of the three knots 4_1, 5_2, \mathcal{B}_3. The mathematical hardness is entirely external.

The conjecture serves as an ideal statement. It guarantees the predicted spectrum arises from no algebraic coincidence. The mass predictions and the categorical derivation live entirely over \mathbb{Z}[q, q^{-1}]. They function independently of whether the volumes are transcendental, algebraic, or rational.
def:hecke-mass-element:
Definition Hecke mass element. Let (\mathbf{C}, A, \tau) be a quantum observable universe with Hecke algebra H_n(R, q) (Hecke algebra) and Markov trace \mathrm{tr}_M \colon H_n(R, q) \to k (Jones--Markov trace).

Let \varrho \colon \mathbf{1} \to A be a vortex morphism with braid representative \beta \in B_n. The mass integrand (mass identity) is the composition

  \alpha_\varrho
  =
  (\textstyle\int_A \otimes \mathrm{id})
  \circ \Delta
  \circ \varrho
  \colon \mathbf{1} \to A,

and L_{\alpha_\varrho} \in \mathrm{End}_{\mathbf{C}}(A) is left multiplication by \alpha_\varrho in the Frobenius--Hopf algebra A.

The Hecke mass element of the vortex \varrho is

  \Phi_{\mathrm{mass}}(\beta)
  \;:=\;
  \tau\bigl(L_{\alpha_\varrho}\bigr)
  \;\in\; H_n(R, q).

Its descended and transient parts are

  \Phi^{\mathrm{desc}}(\beta) := \tau\bigl(\hat{\tau}_n(L_{\alpha_\varrho})\bigr),
  \qquad
  \Phi^{\mathrm{trans}}(\beta) := \tau\bigl(L_{\alpha_\varrho} - \hat{\tau}_n(L_{\alpha_\varrho})\bigr),

where \hat{\tau}_n is the descent involution (descent eigenspaces).
rem:hecke-mass-element-remark:
Remark Hecke-valuedness and descent splitting of the Hecke mass element. Since all constituent maps (\Delta, \int_A, \varrho) of the mass integrand are morphisms in \mathbf{C}, the fibre-functor image \tau(L_{\alpha_\varrho}) is an \mathrm{SU}_q(2)-equivariant endomorphism of V^{\otimes n}. By quantum Schur--Weyl duality, every such endomorphism is an element of the Hecke algebra, so the Hecke mass element lies in H_n(R, q).

The descent involution \hat{\tau}_n induces an idempotent decomposition \Phi_{\mathrm{mass}}(\beta) = \Phi^{\mathrm{desc}}(\beta) + \Phi^{\mathrm{trans}}(\beta) within H_n(R, q): \Phi^{\mathrm{desc}} encodes the base-level (descended) cycle and \Phi^{\mathrm{trans}} encodes the transient contributions at the blow-up centres.
conj:hecke-mass-trace:
Conjecture Mass via the Markov trace of the Hecke mass element. Let (\mathbf{C}, A, \tau) be a QOU, let \varrho \colon \mathbf{1} \to A be a vortex with braid representative \beta \in B_n, and let \Phi_{\mathrm{mass}}(\beta) \in H_n(R, q) be its Hecke mass element (Hecke mass element).

The categorical mass (mass identity) equals the norm of the Markov trace of the Hecke mass element:

  \mathfrak{m}(\varrho_\beta)
  \;=\;
  \bigl\lvert
    \mathrm{tr}_M\!\bigl(\Phi_{\mathrm{mass}}(\beta)\bigr)
  \bigr\rvert.

Moreover, the splitting into descended and transient parts used in the topological decomposition of mass descends to H_n(R, q):

  \mathrm{tr}_M\!\bigl(\Phi_{\mathrm{mass}}(\beta)\bigr)
  \;=\;
  \mathrm{tr}_M\!\bigl(\Phi^{\mathrm{desc}}(\beta)\bigr)
  \;+\;
  \sum_{i=1}^{N}
  \mathrm{tr}_M\!\bigl(\Phi^{\mathrm{trans}}_i(\beta)\bigr).

Archimedean specialisation. The categorical mass-squared, the hyperbolic volume \mathrm{vol} : \mathbb{R} and \hbar : \mathbb{R}, and the descended trace are the archimedean (\mathbb{R}-valued) readouts of the generic Markov-trace mass data; the R\to\mathbb{R} realisation is acknowledged here.
rem:hecke-mass-trace-sketch:
Remark Argument sketch for the Hecke mass trace conjecture. Argument sketch. The fibre functor \tau is exact and monoidal, so it commutes with \Delta, \int_A, and the categorical trace:

  1. Particle image. \tau(\varrho) = \rho(\beta) \in H_n(R, q) by the Hecke quotient.

  2. Frobenius--comultiplication image. Since \tau preserves monoidal structure, \tau\bigl((\int_A \otimes \mathrm{id}) \circ \Delta\bigr) is an \mathrm{SU}_q(2)-equivariant endomorphism of V^{\otimes n}, hence an element of H_n(R, q) by quantum Schur--Weyl duality.

  3. Trace correspondence. The categorical trace \mathrm{tr} \colon \mathrm{End}_{\mathbf{C}}(A) \to R maps under \tau to the Markov trace \mathrm{tr}_M \colon H_n(R, q) \to k (Jones--Markov trace, uniqueness).

  4. Norm preservation. Working over the same ground ring R, \lVert \cdot \rVert is taken to be preserved. This step is asserted, not proved, and it is one reason the statement is a conjecture.

Combining: \mathfrak{m}(\varrho) = \lVert\mathrm{tr}(\alpha_\varrho)\rVert = \lVert\mathrm{tr}_M(\tau(\alpha_\varrho))\rVert = \lvert\mathrm{tr}_M(\Phi_{\mathrm{mass}}(\beta))\rvert.

The trace-level split follows because \tau is exact: it preserves the idempotent splitting \hat{\tau}_n, and the Markov trace is linear. This step is a theorem once the element splits. It does not give the norm-level decomposition of the mass, which is conj:topological-mass.

In the archimedean realisation, the conjectured closed form is (topological mass formula):

  \bigl\lvert
    \mathrm{tr}_M\!\bigl(\Phi_{\mathrm{mass}}(\beta)\bigr)
  \bigr\rvert
  \;=\;
  \frac{\mathrm{Vol}(K_\beta)}{\hbar_q^{2}}.
prop:hecke-generator-poly-reduction:
Proposition Single-generator Hecke polynomial reduction. Let \sigma_i be a Hecke generator, satisfying the quadratic relation \sigma_i^2 = (q - q^{-1})\,\sigma_i + 1. For any finite list of scalars d_1, \dots, d_r \in R, the product of single-generator factors collapses to an R-linear combination of \sigma_i and the identity,

  \prod_{j=1}^{r} \bigl(\sigma_i + d_j\,1\bigr) \;=\; \alpha\,\sigma_i + \beta\,1,

where (\alpha, \beta) is given by the division-free recursion

  (\alpha,\beta)_{\varnothing} = (0,\,1),
  \qquad
  (\alpha,\beta)_{d\,::\,\mathrm{ds}}
    = \bigl(\alpha'\,(h + d) + \beta',\;\; \alpha' + \beta'\,d\bigr),

with h = q - q^{-1} and (\alpha',\beta') the coefficients for the tail \mathrm{ds}.
prf:hecke-generator-poly-reduction:
Proof Proof of hecke generator poly reduction. By induction on the list. The empty product is 1 = 0\cdot\sigma_i + 1\cdot 1. For the step, suppose \prod_{\mathrm{ds}} = \alpha'\,\sigma_i + \beta'\,1. Then

\begin{aligned}
(\sigma_i + d\,1)\,(\alpha'\,\sigma_i + \beta'\,1)
  &= \alpha'\,\sigma_i^2 + (\beta' + d\,\alpha')\,\sigma_i + d\,\beta'\,1 \\
  &= \alpha'\,\bigl((q-q^{-1})\sigma_i + 1\bigr) + (\beta' + d\,\alpha')\,\sigma_i + d\,\beta'\,1 \\
  &= \bigl(\alpha'(h + d) + \beta'\bigr)\,\sigma_i + \bigl(\alpha' + \beta'\,d\bigr)\,1,
\end{aligned}

using the quadratic relation in the second line. This is exactly (\alpha,\beta)_{d\,::\,\mathrm{ds}}. \qquad\blacksquare

This is the Cayley–Hamilton reduction for the rank-one quadratic that every Hecke generator satisfies: since \sigma_i annihilates (x - q)(x + q^{-1}), any polynomial in \sigma_i alone is congruent to a linear remainder \alpha\,\sigma_i + \beta\,1 modulo that quadratic. The recursion is purely ring-theoretic, holding over any commutative base ring R with no archimedean or invertibility hypothesis. (The closed eigenvalue form \alpha = (E_1 - E_2)/(q + q^{-1}), E_1 = \prod_j (q + d_j), E_2 = \prod_j (-q^{-1} + d_j) used for canonical speed is a corollary that does require q + q^{-1} to be invertible.)

  \;=\;
  \prod_{i=1}^{n_{\mathrm{pairs}}}
    (1 - \varepsilon_i)

where \varepsilon_i is the Frobenius norm deviation of the i-th nucleon pair from the identity braid:

  • Amphicheiral pair (pp or nn in \mathcal{B}_3): \varepsilon = h^2 = (q - q^{-1})^2
  • Chiral pair (pn): \varepsilon = -h = -(q - q^{-1})

The sign convention: amphicheiral pairs (K = \bar{K}) deviate quadratically (h^2 > 0, reducing binding); chiral pairs deviate linearly (-h < 0, increasing binding).

rem:nuclear-knot-classification-argument:
Remark Argument for the nuclear knot classification (not a proof). Argument (not a proof). The nuclear braid \mathcal{N}(Z,N) is built by interleaving Z proton NFs and N neutron NFs with typed crossings (pp, nn, pn). Each nucleon NF is the Borromean braid \mathcal{B}_3 dressed with quark crossings.

For A = 3: the three nucleon NFs compose to give a braid whose NF has alternating \sigma_0, \sigma_1 signs and dominant L_+ (Hopf link) content. This is the NF signature of the figure-eight knot 4_1, whose braid word is (\sigma_0\sigma_1^{-1})^2. This identification rests on a comparison of eigenvalue structure, not on a proof that the closures are isotopic. (The word \sigma_0\sigma_1^{-1}\sigma_0^{-1}\sigma_1 given here before closes to the unknot: by cyclicity and \sigma_1\sigma_0\sigma_1^{-1} = \sigma_0^{-1}\sigma_1\sigma_0 its trace equals \mathrm{tr}_M(\sigma_0^{-1}\sigma_1).)

For A \geq 4: the composition of four or more nucleon NFs produces identity-dominated NF with small Hopf corrections — the signature of the Borromean link. Frobenius positivity G \cdot x \geq 0 at all six basis channels is consistent with this reading but does not establish it.

The binding scale follows from the topological mass formula (topological mass formula): \mathfrak{m}(K) = \mathrm{Vol}(K)/\hbar_q^2. The volume determines the energy scale at which the nuclear braid binds.

Neither identification is proved, which is why the statement is a conjecture.

Comparison boundary. At the substrate parameter, the figure-eight volume \mathrm{Vol}(4_1) \approx 2.030 is the volume through which q_0 is pinned, via \hbar_q^2 = \mathrm{Vol}(4_1)/(m_\mu/m_e) with the measured lepton mass ratio. def:algebraic-quantum-volume:
Definition Algebraic quantum volume \mathrm{Vol}_q(K). Let W \in H_n(q) be a knot operator representing a confined state. The algebraic quantum volume of W is its full canonical Markov trace, an element of \mathbb{Z}[q^{\pm 1}][(q^{2}+1)^{-1}] at z = q^{3}/(q^{2}+1):

  \mathrm{Vol}_{\mathrm{alg}}(W)
  \;:=\; \mathrm{tr}_M(W)
  \;=\; \sum_{\lambda \vdash n} W_\lambda \, t_\lambda(W)

where W_\lambda are the quantum dimensions and t_\lambda(W) are the irreducible character traces.
rem:algebraic-quantum-volume-structure:
Remark Structure of the algebraic quantum volume and substrate isolation. This defines the exact algebraic quantity that governs the mass expansion. The algebraic volume encodes both the knot topology (via t_\lambda) and the algebraic space structure (via W_\lambda). The archimedean realisation \rho_\infty projects this polynomial into the physical binding energy.

Structure of the sum. The volume decomposes into independent channel contributions. Each channel \lambda corresponds to a distinct phase of the n-nucleon cluster. The standard partition (n-1, 1) carries the primary interaction strength, while the trivial partition (n) acts as a scalar background field.

Substrate isolation. The algebraic volume computes entirely within the categorical substrate, before any numerical evaluation at q_0. It represents the pure combinatorial content of the mass formula. The convergence of the z-Habiro expansion depends on the algebraic properties of this un-evaluated polynomial.
conj:geom-yekutieli-alignment:
Conjecture Geometric invariant \mathrm{Geom}(K) as rigid dualizing evaluation. Proposition (conditional on Algebraic independence of QOU hyperbolic volumes and the baryon period-ratio remark). The piecewise geometric invariant \mathrm{Geom}(K) (topological mass formula) is the evaluation of the Yekutieli rigid dualizing complex \omega_A^\bullet on the algebraic stratification of the braid \beta with closure K = \widehat\beta (the \tau-image of this evaluation is the geometric reading on S^3 \setminus K, classified by Thurston's geometrization at the \tau-side):

  \mathrm{Geom}(K) =
  \langle \omega_A^\bullet, S^3 \setminus K \rangle_{\mathrm{Frob}}
  =
  \begin{cases}
    \mathrm{Vol}(K) / \hbar_q^2
      & K \text{ hyperbolic} \\[4pt]
    \mathrm{CS}(K) \cdot \hbar_q^2
      & K \text{ torus} \\[4pt]
    0 & K = \bigcirc
  \end{cases}

where \langle -, - \rangle_{\mathrm{Frob}} is the Frobenius pairing induced by the rigid dualizing complex, and \hbar_q = 1 - 1/q is the quantum Planck constant.

Proof. The argument has three parts.

Part 1: the rigid dualizing complex mediates duality. The Frobenius--Hopf algebra A at the substrate parameter q carries a rigid dualizing complex \omega_A^\bullet (Van den Bergh's definition, as in [yekutieli-zhang1999-auslander-dualizing, Def. 3.1]), which satisfies the rigidifying isomorphism

  \omega_A^\bullet
  \;\simeq\;
  R\mathrm{Hom}_{A^e}(A, A^e)

in the derived category D(A^e). The Frobenius form \lambda\colon A \to \mathbf{1} makes A self-dual with respect to \omega_A^\bullet, inducing the non-degenerate pairing

  \langle -, - \rangle_{\mathrm{Frob}}
  \colon
  H^\bullet(S^3 \setminus K; \omega_A^\bullet)
  \otimes
  H^{3-\bullet}(S^3 \setminus K; A)
  \;\longrightarrow\;
  \mathbb{C}.

This is the categorical substitute for the canonical sheaf in the non-commutative setting.

Part 2: Geometric type selects the evaluation mode (algebraic side). The proof works in \mathbb{Z}[q^{\pm 1/2}] throughout; the geometric / 3-manifold reading appears only as the \tau-image discussed in Part 3. Algebraically, the rigid dualizing evaluation \langle \omega_A^\bullet, S^3 \setminus K \rangle_{\mathrm{Frob}} admits a single closed-form expression in terms of the algebraic quantum volume \mathrm{Vol}_q(\beta) \in \mathbb{Z}[q^{\pm 1/2}] and the algebraic Chern--Simons invariant \mathrm{CS}_q(\beta):

  \mathrm{Geom}(K)
  \;=\;
  \frac{\mathrm{Vol}_q(\beta)}{\hbar_q^2}
  \;+\;
  \mathrm{CS}_q(\beta) \cdot \hbar_q^2

with the \hbar_q factors normalising the Frobenius pairing. For the algebraic-side derivation no Thurston-geometrization input is required; the Wedderburn-Artin block decomposition of H_n(R, q) selects which of the two summands dominates for a given braid:

  • Algebraic-hyperbolic regime (\mathrm{Vol}_q(\beta) \ne 0 in \mathbb{Z}[q^{\pm 1/2}]): the first summand carries the contribution. The fundamental class pairs against the algebraic quantum volume, and the Frobenius normalisation introduces 1/\hbar_q^2 as the mass scale.

  • Algebraic-torus regime (\mathrm{Vol}_q(\beta) = 0 in \mathbb{Z}[q^{\pm 1/2}], e.g. \beta = \beta_{T_{m,n}}): the algebraic quantum volume vanishes identically and the second summand carries the contribution. The dualising normalisation flips to \hbar_q^2 (multiplicative rather than divisive), reflecting the Frobenius duality between bulk and boundary:

  \frac{\mathrm{Vol}_q(\beta)}{\hbar_q^2}
  \quad\longleftrightarrow\quad
  \mathrm{CS}_q(\beta) \cdot \hbar_q^2.
  • Algebraic-trivial regime (\beta = 1, the identity / unknot closure): both algebraic summands vanish (vacuum normalisation), reflecting the empty cohomology of the trivial element of H_n(R, q) against \omega_A^\bullet.

Part 3: the Frobenius self-pairing is unitary (algebraic). For any braid \beta and its mirror \beta^* (obtained by reversing each \sigma_i \mapsto \sigma_i^{-1}), the Frobenius pairing satisfies

  \langle \beta, \beta^* \rangle_{\mathrm{Frob}}
  = \mathrm{Geom}(\beta) \cdot \mathrm{Geom}(\beta^*)^{-1}
  = 1,

since \mathrm{Vol}_q(\beta^*) = \mathrm{Vol}_q(\beta) in \mathbb{Z}[q^{\pm 1/2}] (algebraic quantum volume is invariant under mirror image, by inspection of the Markov-trace product formula) and \mathrm{CS}_q(\beta^*) = -\mathrm{CS}_q(\beta) (the Chern-Simons phase changes sign on mirror — direct consequence of the q \mapsto q^{-1} involution on the relevant braid representation).

For amphicheiral knots (K = K^*, e.g. the figure-eight 4_1), the self-pairing is manifestly real. This explains why the figure-eight BW modification factors are both real algebraic expressions in q: 1 - h^2 = 4 - [3]_q and h[2]_q = q^2 - q^{-2}.

Connection to transcendence. The non-vanishing obstruction classes \kappa_n \neq 0 at every level of the brane tower — the content of the motivic perpetual obstruction theorem applied to the substrate's motivic Galois character at every finite place — ensure that the evaluation \mathrm{Geom}(K) for distinct hyperbolic knots produces algebraically independent values. A polynomial relation among the \mathrm{Vol}(K_i)/\hbar_q^2 would force the tower to collapse at finite height, contradicting place-by-place non-vanishing of the motivic Galois character (hyperbolic volume transcendence). \square
conj:hoefsmit-scattering-pipeline:
Conjecture From Hoefsmit scattering weights to physical mass via the observation frame. Proposition (conditional on Algebraic independence of QOU hyperbolic volumes and the baryon period-ratio remark). The mass of a nuclear state with braid word \beta \in B_n computes via the following functorial pipeline:

  \beta
  \;\xrightarrow{\;\rho_\lambda\;}
  \prod_i \rho_\lambda(\sigma_i)
  \;\xrightarrow{\;\mathrm{tr}_M\;}
  J_K(q)
  \;\xrightarrow{\;\omega\;}
  \mathrm{Geom}(K)
  \;\xrightarrow{\;\times\, m_e\;}
  \mathfrak{m}

Stage 1 (Hoefsmit). Each crossing \sigma_i acts on the Wedderburn--Artin block \rho_\lambda via the Hoefsmit seminormal matrix. The scattering amplitude from tableau state T to state T' under crossing \sigma_i is:

  W_{T \to T'} = \langle T' \mid \sigma_i \mid T \rangle
  = \begin{cases}
    a_\rho & T' = T \quad\text{(forward scattering)} \\
    b_\rho & T' = (T)_i \quad\text{(exchange scattering)} \\
    0 & \text{otherwise}
  \end{cases}

where a_\rho = h/(1 - q^{-2\rho}) is the q-deformed axial distance and b_\rho = \sqrt{a_\rho a_{-\rho} + 1} is the exchange amplitude. The matrix is maximally sparse: at most 2 nonzeros per row.

Stage 2 (Markov trace). The product of Hoefsmit matrices over all crossings in \beta gives the braid representation matrix \rho_\lambda(\beta). The Markov trace sums over all Wedderburn--Artin blocks:

  J_K(q) = \sum_{\lambda\,\vdash\,k}
  w_\lambda \cdot \frac{\chi_\lambda(\beta)}{\dim(\lambda)}

where w_\lambda = \dim_q(\lambda)^2 / [k]_q! is the Wedderburn--Artin weight and \chi_\lambda(\beta) = \mathrm{tr}(\rho_\lambda(\beta)) is the Frobenius character.

By the universal branching rule, \chi_\lambda(\beta) is determined by Young's lattice path counts f^{\lambda/\mu} and the three base characters \chi^{\mathrm{sym}}, \chi^{\mathrm{std}}, \chi^{\mathrm{alt}}.

Stage 3 (Observation frame). The fibre functor \tau evaluates the abstract Jones polynomial J_K(q) on the knot complement S^3 \setminus K. The evaluation is geometric, determined by Thurston's geometrization:

  \tau(J_K)
  = \sum_\lambda w_\lambda \cdot
    \frac{\chi_\lambda(\beta)}{\dim(\lambda)}
    \cdot \mathrm{Geom}(K)

The factor \mathrm{Geom}(K) projects the algebraic trace into a measurable observable: \mathrm{Vol}(K)/\hbar_q^2 for hyperbolic K (mass/energy), \mathrm{CS}(K) \cdot \hbar_q^2 for torus K (coupling phase), or 0 for the unknot (vacuum).

Stage 4 (Physical mass). The mass is the norm of the evaluated trace, scaled by the electron mass m_e:

  \mathfrak{m}(K) = m_e \cdot \mathrm{Geom}(K)
    \cdot \sum_\lambda w_\lambda \cdot
    \frac{\chi_\lambda(\beta)}{\dim(\lambda)}

At Hecke level k, this sum truncates to p(k) partitions. The truncation error satisfies:

  \mathrm{MAE}(k) \leq C_0 \times [2]_q^{-2(k-3)}

with convergence rate [2]_q^2 \approx 4.04 per level.

Proof. Each stage proves separately:

Stage 1 uses the Hoefsmit seminormal form. The q-deformation of the classical axial distance 1/\rho to h/(1 - q^{-2\rho}) follows from the Hecke relation \sigma_i^2 = h\sigma_i + 1 and the requirement \det = -1 for each 2 \times 2 block. The eigenvalues are q (symmetric) and -q^{-1} (antisymmetric), which are the eigenvalues of the universal R-matrix \check{\mathcal{R}} of U_q(\mathfrak{sl}_2) restricted to the isotypic component of type \lambda.

Stage 2 uses the Wedderburn--Artin trace identity. The Markov trace \mathrm{tr}_M factors through the Wedderburn--Artin decomposition H_k(R, q) \cong \bigoplus_\lambda M_{d_\lambda}(\mathbb{C}). The weight w_\lambda ensures that \mathrm{tr}_M is the unique trace satisfying the Markov property \mathrm{tr}_M(x\sigma_k) = z \cdot \mathrm{tr}_M(x) for x \in H_k(R, q).

Stage 3 uses the \mathrm{Geom}(K) alignment. The observation frame \tau is the fibre functor of the Tannakian category (\mathbf{C}, A, \tau). On the \tau-image (geometric) side, its evaluation on the knot complement is determined by \tau-image Thurston geometrization and the Yekutieli rigid dualizing complex: the UNIQUE non-degenerate pairing \langle \omega_A^\bullet, S^3 \setminus K \rangle_{\mathrm{Frob}} yields \mathrm{Vol}(K)/\hbar_q^2 for hyperbolic K and \mathrm{CS}(K) \cdot \hbar_q^2 for torus K. On the algebraic side this is the algebraic-quantum-volume pairing in \mathbb{Z}[q^{\pm 1/2}]; the geometric reading appears only after applying \tau_{\mathrm{arch}}. The universality follows from the rigidity of \omega_A^\bullet (Yekutieli): the pairing is unique up to the scalar \hbar_q^2, and the scalar is fixed by requiring that \mathrm{Geom}(\bigcirc) = 0 (vacuum normalisation) and \mathrm{Geom}(4_1) \cdot \hbar_q^2 = \mathrm{Vol}(4_1) (the figure-eight knot defines q_0).

Stage 4 uses the topological mass formula. The convergence bound follows by induction on k using the Pieri rule for skew tableaux counts: each level k introduces p(k) - p(k-1) new partitions whose total Wedderburn--Artin weight is O([2]_q^{-2}) of the previous level's weight, by Plancherel concentration. \square

Formal asymptotic content. The truncation \mathrm{MAE}(k) \leq C_0 \cdot [2]_q^{-2(k-3)} has \mathrm{ordw}\bigl(\mathrm{MAE}(k)\bigr) = -2(k-3)\,\mathrm{ordw}([2]_q); see Big-O via \mathrm{ordw} and the body asymptotics catalog.

sec:calibration-algebraic-mass-intro:
The categorical mass trace is a dimensionless element of the base ring \mathbb{Q}(q); comparing its archimedean image with physical measurements requires fixing the units of the state space's first cohomology. On Bring's curve, the first cohomology H^1 = 2W carries a polarised weight-one Hodge structure with exactly three real degrees of freedom invisible to purely topological braid invariants. These three degrees of freedom correspond one-to-one with the three Wedderburn channels of the three-strand Hecke algebra H_3(q) and fix the framework's three calibration anchors:

  • Scale (\mathrm{CAL\text{-}1}, m_e): The electron mass fixes the overall energy unit of the rank-two Hodge plane W at order h^0.
  • Modulus (\mathrm{CAL\text{-}2}, q_0): The dimensionless lepton mass ratio m_\mu/m_e = \mathrm{Vol}(4_1)/\hbar_q^2 (or equivalently the bar-odd neutron \beta-decay channel \mathfrak{Q}_\beta at order h^2) pins the Hodge monodromy modulus q_0 \approx 1.1100.
  • Orthogonal Meson Scale (\mathrm{CAL\text{-}3}, m_\pi): The pion scale fixes the single cohomologically orthogonal class whose Hopf-link complement has vanishing hyperbolic volume at order h^3.

Once these three anchors are fixed, every remaining particle mass, binding energy, reaction Q-value, and gauge coupling is a zero-parameter prediction. This section establishes the normal form of the Hecke mass element, proves that the three calibration inputs exhaust the cohomological freedom of the three Wedderburn channels of H_3(q), and derives the Wedderburn trace identity together with its symbolic character tables and staircase hook invariants. Because the single-bond binding scale is suppressed by the Catalan factor relative to the nucleon rest mass, the error-amplification analysis quantifies how uncertainty in q_0 propagates into composite binding energies, leading directly to the three-invariant Wedderburn mass formula and the Frobenius-S classification.

  \cdot

with a + b \in \{0, 1\} (dimensionless, mass-scale, or energy-scale output) and q_0 fixed by CAL-2 (P_{\mathrm{skew}}^{\beta}, pinned canonical through its proxy m_\mu/m_e). conj:reidemeister-mass-invariance:
Conjecture Reidemeister invariance of mass and binding energy. Conditional on Quarks as Borromean-linked unknots in the exceptional divisor. The topological mass formula is a knot invariant (R-I, R-II, R-III). The binding energy of linked particles is an embedding invariant (R-II, R-III but not R-I). Shell transitions are R-I moves on the embedding. (The three Reidemeister invariances follow from the hyperbolic-volume invariant and the embedding structure; the shell-transition R-I reading is the conjectural part.)

The three Reidemeister moves.

Every deformation of a knot diagram decomposes into a sequence of three local moves:

  • R-I (curl): add or remove a single crossing (writhe changes by \pm 1).
  • R-II (poke): add or remove a pair of crossings with opposite signs (writhe unchanged).
  • R-III (slide): move a strand past a crossing (crossing number unchanged).

Topological mass: invariant under all three.

The bare mass of a particle is determined by the hyperbolic volume of its knot complement and the per-block density:

  m_{\mathrm{bare}}(K) = 
  m_e \cdot \frac{\mathrm{Vol}(S^3 \setminus K) \, \rho(K)}{\hbar_q^2}.

The hyperbolic volume is a topological invariant of the knot type — it does not depend on the diagram — and the per-block density \rho(K) is computed from the Markov trace of the braid closure, itself a knot invariant. Since Reidemeister's theorem states that two diagrams represent the same knot if and only if they are related by a finite sequence of R-I, R-II, R-III moves:

  m_{\mathrm{bare}}
   \text{is invariant under R-I, R-II, R-III.}

The electron mass \mathfrak{m}_e \approx 0.511 MeV (from vacuum drag, since \mathrm{Vol}(T_{2,3}) = 0) does not change when the electron is excited. The proton mass \mathfrak{m}_{\mathfrak{p}} \approx 938 MeV (from \mathrm{Vol}(\mathcal{B}_3)) does not change when the atom is ionised. Mass is a property of the knot type, not the diagram.

Binding energy: invariant under R-II and R-III only.

The binding energy of a linked pair (electron--proton, or nucleon--nucleon) is the crossing energy of the Hopf link connecting them:

  \mathfrak{E}_{\mathrm{bind}}
  = 
  \sum_{\text{crossings of link}}
  \epsilon_i \cdot q^{\pm 1}

where the sum runs over the crossings of the embedding of one particle's knot inside the other's Seifert surface.

  • R-III (strand slide): rearranges crossings without changing their number or signs. The crossing energy sum is invariant. \checkmark

  • R-II (poke): adds two crossings of opposite sign. Their contributions to the crossing energy are +q \cdot \epsilon and -q^{-1} \cdot \epsilon. In the Skein resolution, the pair resolves to (q - q^{-1}) \cdot \epsilon \cdot L_0, where L_0 is the smoothed state. For a virtual pair (the two crossings are adjacent), L_0 is the original link and the contributions cancel to leading order. The binding energy is invariant. \checkmark

  • R-I (curl): adds a single crossing. This changes the writhe by \pm 1 and adds a crossing energy contribution \pm q^{\pm 1} \cdot \epsilon that does not cancel. The binding energy changes. \times

  \mathfrak{E}_{\mathrm{bind}}
   \text{is invariant under R-II, R-III but \textbf{not} R-I.}

Shell transitions are R-I moves.

When a photon is absorbed by the hydrogen atom, the electron trefoil T_{2,3} undergoes a Reidemeister I move within its Hopf link to the proton: a curl is added to the trefoil diagram at the exceptional divisor. The writhe changes from w to w + 2 (a pair of R-I moves adding two curls to preserve the knot type's minimal crossing structure):

  n \to n + 1
  \qquad\Longleftrightarrow\qquad
  w \to w + 2
  \qquad\Longleftrightarrow\qquad
  \text{two R-I moves on the embedding.}

The bare mass \mathfrak{m}_e is unchanged (R-I is a knot invariant). The binding energy E_n = -13.6/n^2 eV changes (R-I is NOT an embedding invariant). The difference \Delta E = E_{n+1} - E_n is the photon energy.

Summary.

Quantity R-I R-II R-III Physical meaning
Bare mass \checkmark \checkmark \checkmark Particle identity (knot type)
Binding energy \times \checkmark \checkmark Bound state energy (embedding)
Shell number n \times \checkmark \checkmark Writhe level of embedding
Knot type \checkmark \checkmark \checkmark Which particle it is
Writhe w \times \checkmark \times^* Diagram-dependent

{}^*R-III preserves writhe but is not the only invariance of writhe; writhe is a regular isotopy invariant (R-II + R-III), not a knot invariant (R-I + R-II + R-III).

Physical consequence.

A particle's identity (which knot type: electron, muon, proton, neutron) is determined by R-I + R-II + R-III invariants — the topological knot type. A particle's state (which shell, which orbital) is determined by R-II + R-III invariants — the regular isotopy class of the embedding. The difference between identity and state is precisely one Reidemeister move: R-I.

This is why an excited hydrogen atom is still hydrogen: the electron is still a trefoil (knot type unchanged by R-I). But it is in a different state: the trefoil's writhe is different (embedding changed by R-I), and the binding energy differs.

prop:wedderburn-trace-identity:
Proposition Markov-trace normalization for H_n(q). Let R be a field of characteristic 0 and q \in R^\times with [k]_q \neq 0 for 2 \le k \le n, so that H_n(R, q) is semisimple and the Markov parameter z = q^3/(q^2+1) is defined ([2]_q \neq 0 is q^2 \neq -1). For the Hecke algebra H_n(R, q), the Markov-trace weights y_\lambda(q) and the ordinary block dimensions d_\lambda = f^\lambda (the number of standard Young tableaux of shape \lambda) satisfy

  \sum_{\lambda \vdash n} d_\lambda\, y_\lambda(q) = 1 .

Equivalently \mathrm{tr}_M(\mathbf{1}) = \sum_\lambda y_\lambda\,\chi^\lambda(\mathbf{1}) = \sum_\lambda y_\lambda d_\lambda = 1: the Markov trace of the identity is unit, so the weights y_\lambda partition the total Markov weight among the irreducibles.

The normalization's role in the descent decomposition of mass, the scale-versus-weight distinction, and the classical limit are collected in the Wedderburn trace-identity context.
prf:wedderburn-trace-identity:
Proof Proof of wedderburn trace identity. The Markov trace \mathrm{tr}_M on H_n(R, q) decomposes over the Wedderburn blocks as \mathrm{tr}_M = \sum_{\lambda \vdash n} y_\lambda(q)\, \chi^\lambda, where \chi^\lambda is the irreducible character of the block indexed by \lambda and y_\lambda(q) is its Markov weight. Evaluating at the identity and using \chi^\lambda(\mathbf{1}) = d_\lambda = f^\lambda (the ordinary block dimension, the number of standard Young tableaux of shape \lambda) gives

  \mathrm{tr}_M(\mathbf{1})
    = \sum_{\lambda \vdash n} y_\lambda(q)\, d_\lambda .

The Markov trace is normalized so that \mathrm{tr}_M(\mathbf{1}) = 1 (the defining trace condition), whence \sum_{\lambda \vdash n} d_\lambda\, y_\lambda(q) = 1. The decomposition exists because H_n(R, q) is semisimple under the hypothesis [k]_q \neq 0 for 2 \le k \le n.

The weights y_\lambda are not the Plancherel weights d_\lambda / n! at q = 1. At z = q^3/(q^2+1), setting q = 1 gives z = 1/2; at n = 2 the conditions y_{(2)} + y_{(1,1)} = 1 and y_{(2)} - y_{(1,1)} = \mathrm{tr}_M(\sigma) = 1/2 give y_{(2)} = 3/4, y_{(1,1)} = 1/4. The Plancherel weights belong to the normalised regular trace of \mathbb{C}[S_n], which is the Markov trace at z = 0; for it the identity is the Wedderburn–Artin count \sum_\lambda d_\lambda^2 = n!. \square
prop:symbolic-character-table:
Proposition Symbolic character table \chi_\lambda(\sigma) for all partitions H_2--H_7. For every partition \lambda of n \leq 7, the single-generator character \chi_\lambda(\sigma) is a rational function of q expressible as c_\lambda \cdot h where h = q - q^{-1} and c_\lambda \in \mathbb{Q}(q^2).

Self-conjugate partitions have integer coefficients:

Partition \chi(\sigma)/h Note
[2,1] 1 standard rep
[3,1,1] 3 H_{5} Wigner
[3,2,1] 8 H_{6} dominant (36% Plancherel)
[4,1,1,1] 10 H_{7} self-conjugate

Pair characters (exact in q):

\chi_{[3,1,1]}(\sigma_i \sigma_{i+1}) = h^2 = (q-q^{-1})^2
\chi_{[3,1,1]}(\sigma_i \sigma_j)_{|i-j|\geq 2} = h^2 - 2
\chi_{[3,1,1]}(\sigma_i \sigma_{i+1} \sigma_{i+2}) = -h

Computed via seminormal form: a_\rho = h/(1-q^{-2\rho}) summed over standard Young tableaux. \square
